name: Ulsena

anatomy.part: holdfast: root base where the stem meets the spreading roots
heart: centre of the broad stalk body
stalk: upper part of the stem, under the veil
crown float: top of the bell-shaped veil
crown frond: the veil's trailing tail on the right
upper left frond: junction of the left ribbon frond
long left tip: end of the long left ribbon
small left tip: end of the short left ribbon
long right tip: end of the long right ribbon
lower right tip: end of the hanging right frond
base frond: lower left ribbon frond near the root
base frond tip: end of the lower left ribbon
lower left frond: short ribbon branching off the stem

myth: Ulsena was a kelp-woman who lived in the cold shallows under the cliffs. One hot, calm day, which the old ones say never comes here, she climbed onto the rocks and married Ristan, a fisherman of the north skerry. He went out the next spring and the gale Tavo came laughing across the water and took his boat. Ulsena waited in the shallows. When no boat came back she did what kelp does when it wants the light. She grew. Her stalk went up past the seals, past the gulls, and when it left the water it kept going, because Aun had cut the string and nothing held the sky down any more. Her bulb is the crown at the top. Her long brown fronds still sway in the Unflown. Mother Hesk counts her turns and says she has not yet found him. Sailors say that on a calm night, if you hear a slow creak over the water, it is Ulsena, still looking.
verse:
Her stalk climbs past gulls,
through the cut string's empty air,
she sways, still searching.
